title: Benjamin Netanyahu returns as Israel’s prime minister
description_short: Israel’s 37th government, led by Benjamin Netanyahu, was sworn in on December 29, 2022.
description_medium: The Knesset records that Israel’s 37th government was sworn in on December 29, 2022, with Benjamin Netanyahu presenting its policy guidelines. Reuters reported his return at the head of a hard-right cabinet. The frozen record’s 2009 date is wrong for this return. The claimed Trump or Kushner connection remains unverified.
description_long: This internal draft narrows the event to Benjamin Netanyahu’s return as Israel’s prime minister. The frozen record dates that return to March 31, 2009, but the supplied reporting and official Knesset record identify the relevant government formation as December 29, 2022. The Knesset says the 37th Government was sworn in that day, Netanyahu presented its policy guidelines, and the confidence vote passed 63 to 54. Reuters described his return at the head of a hard-right cabinet that promised to expand settlements in the occupied West Bank. Those sources support the corrected date and government-formation facts. They do not show that Donald Trump caused, directed, or participated in the 2022 event. The frozen record’s description of Netanyahu as Jared Kushner’s family friend has no supporting citation in the supplied packet and is not established by the Knesset release or the Reuters report used here. Keep that relationship and the entry’s relevance to a Trump-focused collection unresolved. This draft preserves a possible contextual entry for editorial review; it is not publication eligible until its Trump nexus and category are established.

title: Unverified claim: Trump administration ended multiple CIA covert programs
description_short: The supplied record alleges a broad February 2025 shutdown of CIA covert programs; the scope and rationale remain unverified.
description_medium: The frozen entry alleges that the administration ended covert CIA programs across several countries for budgetary and political reasons. Its claims about counter-proliferation, human intelligence, influence operations, and benefits to Russia or China are not independently supported here. Reuters reporting on other Mexico programs does not establish this broad shutdown.
description_long: This internal draft preserves the supplied allegation that the Trump administration terminated multiple CIA covert-action programs in February 2025. The frozen text specifically alleges effects on counter-proliferation work, human-intelligence networks, and influence operations, and attributes the decisions to cost cutting and deference to foreign governments. It further characterizes the alleged changes as a strategic benefit to Moscow and Beijing. These remain claims from the supplied record, not established facts: the packet gives no program names, country-specific notices, decision documents, officials’ statements, or source excerpts that verify the scope, date, motives, or consequences. The date of February 15, 2025 is retained from the original record as an unverified starting date. Reuters reporting located during this review describes the CIA moving resources and personnel to expand counternarcotics work focused on Mexico. Separate Reuters coverage concerns a pause in State Department anti-narcotics assistance in Mexico, which is not the same agency or activity as CIA covert action. Neither report proves that other CIA programs did or did not end. Keep allegations attributed and do not state a global shutdown, its motives, or a strategic windfall as fact pending program-specific evidence.

title: New York judge finds Trump defendants used false financial data to secure lower loan rates
description_short: A 2024 New York civil ruling found false financial statements were used to obtain financing on more favorable terms.
description_medium: In a February 2024 civil fraud ruling, a New York judge found that Trump and related defendants submitted false financial data to obtain financing on more favorable terms. The decision concerns statements and lending terms for entity borrowing. It does not establish that the Trump Organization lent money to Trump personally or that a loan scheme shifted his taxable income.
description_long: This repair is limited to the February 2024 New York Supreme Court decision in the state’s civil fraud case. After a nonjury trial, Justice Arthur Engoron found the defendants liable and wrote that they had submitted false financial data to obtain borrowing at lower rates. The decision describes Trump-controlled entities borrowing from banks and other lenders, with lenders requiring personal guarantees from Trump based on statements of financial condition. The source-supported event is the court’s finding about financial statements and lending terms. It is not a finding that the Trump Organization loaned money to Trump personally at artificially favorable rates, and the sources reviewed do not establish that such loans shifted income or minimized tax liability. Those distinct assertions from the frozen entry are excluded from this card. The corrected date identifies the 2024 ruling, rather than treating 2012 as the date of the court finding. The record does not state a measured public loss, so none is inferred here.

source_fact_map.fact: The trial court found defendants liable and said they submitted false financial data in order to borrow more and at lower rates.
source_fact_map.quote: In order to borrow more and at lower rates, defendants submitted blatantly false financial data to the accountants, resulting in fraudulent financial statements.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Decision and Order After Non-Jury Trial, summary: Donald Trump and entities he controls own many valuable properties. The entities borrowed from banks and other lenders. Lenders required personal guarantees from Donald Trump based on statements of financial condition. In order to borrow more and at lower rates, defendants submitted blatantly false financial data to the accountants, resulting in fraudulent financial statements. The Court states that it now finds defendants liable.

source_fact_map.source_excerpt: February 16, 2024. New York Attorney General Letitia James stated that Justice Arthur F. Engoron of New York State Supreme Court ruled in her favor in her office’s civil fraud case against Donald Trump, the other individual defendants, and the Trump Organization entities. title: ICE solicitation sought online monitoring and facial-recognition capability
description_short: A February 2025 report described an ICE contractor solicitation for social-media monitoring and facial-recognition capability.
description_medium: On February 11, 2025, The Intercept reported that ICE was soliciting contractor proposals to monitor online discussion of the agency and its leaders. The contract documents also requested facial-recognition capability to search for information about a photographed subject. The source describes a proposed procurement, not a deployed mass-identification system, and does not establish targeting of undocumented immigrants or political dissenters.
description_long: This repair narrows the frozen entry to a contractor solicitation reported by The Intercept on February 11, 2025. The article, citing contract documents, says ICE planned to monitor and locate negative social-media discussion about the agency and senior officials. It also quotes a request for facial-recognition capability that could use a subject’s photograph to search the internet for associated information. Those details support a proposal for online monitoring and identity research. They do not establish that a system was awarded, deployed, or used to identify undocumented immigrants across multiple platforms. The source also does not establish that ICE selected political dissenters as targets; it describes monitoring discussion of ICE and its leadership and frames the procurement around threats to personnel and facilities. The original card’s claims of a live mass-identification program, database matching, and disproportionate targeting are therefore removed. This is a serious privacy and speech concern at the proposal stage, with implementation and actual effects unresolved.

source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The document also requests “Facial Recognition capabilities that could take a photograph of a subject and search the internet to find all relevant information associated with the subject.” The contract contains specific directions for targets found in other countries, implying the program would scan the domestic speech of American citizens.
